steps.say: The application finds passages in a document archive, and the model answers from them.
A user asks how the conflict in the Middle East affected Uganda, and how much poverty fell.
The search gives every passage in the archive a score for its closeness in meaning to the question.
The passages are ranked by that score, and the four closest go into the prompt.
All four of those passages are about poverty.
The first passage on the conflict ranks fifth, one place below the cut.
The model reads only the passages in its prompt.
Its answer gives the fall in poverty and states that the passages do not mention the conflict.
The fix divides the question into its two parts and runs one search for each part.
The application merges the two sets of results, so the prompt holds passages on the conflict and on poverty.
With the merged passages, the answer covers both parts, with a citation after each figure.
The answer reports that global energy prices are projected to rise by 24 percent in 2026.
steps.speak: The answer reports that global energy prices are projected to rise by twenty-four percent in twenty twenty-six.

steps.say: The citation leads to page 22 of the June 2026 edition of the Uganda Economic Update.
steps.speak: The citation leads to page twenty-two of the June twenty twenty-six edition of the Uganda Economic Update.
